name: Hiel the Bethelite
charge: Building Jericho again under the oath Joshua adjured before the Lord
summary: When the walls of Jericho fell and the city was burned, Joshua laid an oath on Israel before the Lord: the man who rose up and rebuilt Jericho would lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son (Joshua 6:20-26). The study notes put it plainly: the city was not to be rebuilt. In the days of Ahab, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt it, laying the foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up the gates in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord by Joshua (1 Kings 16:34).
offenseFull: Jericho was shut tight against Israel, with its garrison and walls, and the battle was decided before it began: the Lord told Joshua He had given the city, its king and its mighty men into his hand (Joshua 6:1-2). The people compassed it as the Lord commanded, the priests blew the trumpets, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat (Joshua 6:20). They took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, burnt it with fire, brought the silver, gold, brass and iron into the treasury of the house of the Lord, and saved Rahab and her household because she hid the messengers (Joshua 6:21-25). History in the AM reads Joshua’s charge that the city and all in it were devoted to the Lord, and that Israel must keep itself from the accursed thing lest it trouble the camp (Joshua 6:17-19).

Then Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed before the Lord would be the man who rose up and built the city of Jericho; he would lay its foundation in his firstborn, and set up its gates in his youngest son (Joshua 6:26). The study notes give the plain sense: the city was not to be rebuilt. A word spoken before the Lord binds. When a man vows a vow to the Lord or swears an oath to bind his soul, he is not to break his word but do all that he said (Numbers 30:2); the notes on that law add that a vow cannot simply be gone back on with a request for forgiveness afterward.

Generations later, in the days of Ahab, when the northern kingdom had gone after Baal above all the kings before, Hiel of Bethel built Jericho (1 Kings 16:34). The study notes set his building in the same passage as Ahab’s marriage to Jezebel, his altar to Baal and his grove. He came out of Bethel, where Jeroboam had set up his calf, and he set his hand to a city the Lord had put under a curse.
judgmentFull: He laid the foundation of Jericho in Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by Joshua the son of Nun (1 Kings 16:34). The two ends of the work answered the two parts of the curse exactly as Joshua had spoken it: the firstborn when the foundation was laid, the youngest when the gates were hung. The record gives the names of his sons beside the report that the city was built.

Joshua himself had warned Israel how the word of the Lord works. Near his death he had them acknowledge in all their hearts that not one thing had failed of all the good things the Lord spoke concerning them; all came to pass. The other side is a heavy scripture: as all the good things had come, so the Lord would bring on them all the evil things, until He had destroyed them from the good land, if they transgressed the covenant and served other gods (Joshua 23:14-16). The study notes press it on those who come out of Christianity told that God is good all the time: the Most High also promised to destroy His people when they go off, and that is why Israel is not at home today. Hiel’s sons fell under a word spoken generations before him.

text.text: So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.
But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot’s house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her.

And the young men that were spies went in, and brought out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and all that she had; and they brought out all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel.
And they burnt the city with fire, and all that was therein: only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord.

And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the Lord, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.

In his days did Hiel the Beth–elite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.
Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in.
And the Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour.

So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.

And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

And the city shall be accursed, even it, and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.
And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it.
But all the silver, and gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are consecrated unto the Lord: they shall come into the treasury of the Lord.

And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the Lord, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.
If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.

And, behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts and in all your souls, that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which the Lord your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass unto you, and not one thing hath failed thereof.

Therefore it shall come to pass, that as all good things are come upon you, which the Lord your God promised you; so shall the Lord bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land which the Lord your God hath given you.

When ye have transgressed the covenant of the Lord your God, which he commanded you, and have gone and served other gods, and bowed yourselves to them; then shall the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and ye shall perish quickly from off the good land which he hath given unto you.
And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did more to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him.
